newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK's Williams, Chubb plan lock-up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK's Williams, Chubb plan lock-up.

text.p: Britain's Williams Holdings Plc on Friday launched a recommended 1.3 billion pound ($2.12 billion) offer for Chubb Security Plc in a lock-up that some analysts said was strategic but expensive.
The deal would unite major brand names in the world security industry -- including Yale, Kidde and Chubb -- and create a company with combined annual sales of about 2.7 billion pounds.
"From an industrial point of view, it is an absolutely logical fit," Williams chief executive Roger Carr told Reuters in an interview.

Williams said its strengths in the Americas and continental Europe would get a boost from Chubb's presence in Britain and the Asia-Pacific. The deal would also unlock benefits in purchasing, distribution and plant consolidation.
Conglomerates analysts agreed that the deal made good strategic sense, but some balked at the offer price, which valued Chubb at 450 pence per share.
"The fit is excellent for Williams, but the issue is the price. People think they overpaid. They should have paid maybe 15-16 times earnings, not 21 times," one analyst said.
However, other analysts defended the price.

"It is the price they had to pay to improve the quality of Williams. They will make it pay, but it will take a little longer than perhaps we would have preferred," said Geoff Allum, diversified industrials analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite.
Williams's shares dropped more than 11 percent, falling 36 pence to 302 by 1455 GMT to rank among the top percentage losers on the London Stock Exchange.
Meanwhile, Chubb's shares rose 5.0 pence to 425 in heavy afternoon trade. "The Chubb shareholders have done extremely well," one analyst said.
Williams said its offer represented a 37 percent premium over the closing price of 329.5 pence for Chubb shares on February 11.
Takeover speculation after that date pushed Chubb shares higher in a surge that was being investigated by the London Stock Exchange.
On Thursday, Chubb's stock soared 82 pence, or more than 24 percent, to a year high of 423 pence after the company said it was in talks that might lead to an offer for the group.
Williams's offer -- two new Williams shares and 704.12 pence cash for every three Chubb shares -- consisted of about 50 percent cash and 50 percent stock, the company said.
Williams said it expected to receive regulatory clearance for the deal and overcome any possible monopoly concerns.

"We clearly have issues in that area where there is an overlap, but we are confident that we have solutions to those issues and we're comfortable that we'll achieve a fair and totally acceptable settlement," Carr said.
He added that the deal, which will be partly financed with a 1.0 billion pound credit facility, would be modestly dilutive in the first 12 months. But it would improve earnings thereafter.
Williams forecast an 11 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax pre-exceptional profits to 243 million pounds.
It expected to pay a final dividend of 9.25 pence net, making 15.05 pence for the full year.
Carr noted that Chubb had been one of the attractions behind Williams's failed bid for Racal Electronics Plc, then Chubb's parent, in 1991.
"(Chubb's subsequent demerger) was a response to our bid, but in many ways it created a separate company which became a perfect fit for us later on," he said.
Williams, which also has home improvement operations, did not plan to make further disposals following its recent 360 million pound sale of 15 home products businesses.

"We've got a balanced business. We'll have a billion pounds (in sales) in fire protection, a billion in security and 630 to 640 million in home improvements. And that's a very healthy balance," Carr said. ($1=.6128 Pound)
